clue.text: Showing courage he finally leaves, waving cheerio

indicators.note: waving suggests the letters of the farewell word fluttering into a new order
leaves tells us that a letter departs from the word cheerio
finally points to the last letter of the word he

explanation.surface: A brave man bids goodbye and walks off, waving and calling cheerio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he finally' is E; 'leaves' takes one E out of CHEERIO, leaving CHERIO, and 'waving' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic behaviour is the kind that displays bravery and courage.

clue.text: Girl's artful radiance causing dismay

annotationWithheld.why: Girl's artful radiance causing dismay (10): the only parse is DI + SHEEN full of ART, where 'artful' is both the fodder ART and the container indicator 'full', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Leading Italian politician having regular orgies and about to be put in jail

indicators.note: leading picks out the first letter of the word Italian

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard politician

indicators.note: regular takes every other letter of orgies, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A top Italian politician with a taste for orgies is about to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Regular letters of ORGIES are RIS; 'to be' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up in a jail or prison.

clue.text: No fighting allowed in this old gentlemen's club?

definitions.text: No fighting allowed in this old gentlemen's club?

parts.words: No fighting allowed in this old gentlemen's club?
parts.note: slang for a fusty old man, so an old gentlemen's area reads as a neutral strip between warring sides where combat is forbidden

explanation.surface: A stuffy gentlemen's club bans brawling among its elderly members.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an 'old buffer' is a doddery elderly man, which is the joke behind the 'old gentlemen's club'.
explanation.definitionFit: A demilitarised strip separating hostile forces is exactly a place where fighting is not allowed.

clue.text: Type showing impudent effrontery

definitions.meaning: a heavy, thick typeface used for emphasis in printing
brazen and shameless, describing someone barefaced in their cheek

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a heavy printing typeface and, as an adjective, means brazen or shameless.

clue.text: Intense pressure, then noxious discharge of gas

parts.note: force is pressure or compulsion

indicators.note: discharge of says the gas is let out of the word before it

parts.note: foul means noxious or offensive
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, a gas

explanation.surface: Under great pressure, a smelly gas escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge of' removes oxygen's symbol from the noxious word; 'then' is a link placing the result after the pressure word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forceful is powerful and vigorous, so intense in manner.

clue.text: Girl shrinks and gets lighter in bad relationship

indicators.note: shrinks says the word for the girl gets shorter by a letter

parts.note: miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
a match is something used to light a fire

explanation.surface: A girl loses weight and becomes lighter, all because of a bad relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like a lighter weight; it is a match. 'shrinks' cuts one S from MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mismatch is a pairing of incompatible partners, so a poorly suited relationship.

clue.text: Mucus is brought up in large quantities

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: snot is slang for mucus

explanation.surface: Someone coughs up mucus by the bucketload.
explanation.definitionFit: Tons is an informal plural for great amounts, as in tons of work.

clue.text: When the pope eats stew?

indicators.note: eats says one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: HH, His Holiness, is the pope's title
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about when the pontiff has his stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a stewed or fried dish of chopped meat, close kin to a stew.

clue.text: Old Norse fright masquerading as a work of literature

indicators.note: masquerading means the letters are in disguise, rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: An ancient Scandinavian terror passes itself off as a literary classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of 'Old Norse fright' rearrange into Tolkien's title, whose Norse-flavoured mythology suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's fantasy trilogy is a famous work of literature.

clue.text: See 9
Norman, perhaps, forbids importing oriental vegetables

parts.note: a Norman, from Normandy, is an example of someone French

indicators.note: importing says one piece is brought inside another

parts.note: bans means forbids
E, east, stands for oriental

explanation.surface: A man called Norman bans eastern vegetables from coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like a first name but is a native of Normandy, hence French.
explanation.definitionFit: French beans are green beans eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Blair urges unstable American to carry out illegal invasion for gain

definitions.text: American to carry out illegal invasion for gain
definitions.note: the verb is an Americanism; British English usually says burgle

indicators.note: unstable means the letters of Blair urges are shaky and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Tony Blair presses an erratic American to mount an unlawful invasion for profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Blair and the Iraq War; 'American' belongs to the definition, flagging that the word is US usage for burgle.
explanation.definitionFit: To break into a building to steal is the act described, and this verb form is chiefly American.

clue.text: Ignoring his intermittent treacheries, unwisely reproduce

indicators.note: unwisely suggests the remaining letters are put together badly, in a new order
ignoring means some letters are left out of the word that follows
intermittent says the letters removed are spread through the word, not in one run

explanation.surface: Overlooking his occasional betrayals, someone foolishly makes them happen again.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, I and S out of TREACHERIES, scattered through it, to leave TREACERE, then 'unwisely' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to make it again, so to reproduce it.

clue.text: Refuses to leave corset on couch

parts.note: stays is an old word for a corset
to couch is to put something into words, as in a request couched politely

explanation.surface: Someone will not budge, sprawled on the couch in a corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couch' looks like a sofa but is the verb meaning to express in words; 'on' places it after the corset word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays put remains where they are and declines to move.

clue.text: Flock to see Charlie Sheen in Hollywood

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
luster is the American spelling of lustre, a sheen

explanation.surface: Crowds gather to watch the actor Charlie Sheen in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Sheen the actor is the false trail; 'in Hollywood' asks for the US spelling LUSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To flock is to gather together in a group, as a crowd does.

clue.text: South Sea islander's expression of pleasure captured by European artist

definitions.note: read as 'South Sea islander is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: captured by says the cry of pleasure is held inside the artist's name

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
ah is a sigh of pleasure

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander's sigh of delight is caught on canvas by a European painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry of pleasure sits after the painter's first letter. Gauguin, a European, famously painted Tahitians, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tahiti in French Polynesia is a South Sea islander.

clue.text: Hitman going straight? It's touching

parts.note: read as 'hit' plus 'man': to tan is to hit, and a gent is a man
the second half, man, gives gent, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A hired killer giving up crime makes for a moving story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitman' must be split into 'Hit' and 'man'. 'Going straight' looks like reforming, but a tangent is a straight line that just touches a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: Her felony? To be taken wrongly

definitions.text: Her felony? To be taken wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are set out incorrectly, in a different order

explanation.surface: A woman asks whether her crime was to be carried off unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Greek queen's abduction by Paris was a wrong done to her, not her crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Spartan queen was abducted by Paris, sparking the Trojan War.

clue.text: He touches sensitive organ

definitions.meaning: one who touches or gropes, a toucher
an antenna or tentacle used by animals to sense the world

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a person who touches and also an insect's antenna, a sensitive touch organ.

clue.text: In my sleep I composed a long poem

indicators.note: in says the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A poet claims to have written a lengthy poem while asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is a link word; the run sits across 'slEEP I Composed'. Coleridge's 'Kubla Khan' was famously composed in a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a lengthy narrative poem about heroic deeds.

clue.text: See 4 across
They are weaselly followers of heartless, powerful conspirators

indicators.note: followers of puts the animals after the letters before them
heartless removes the middle letters of powerful, keeping only its ends

parts.note: otters belong to the weasel family, the mustelids

explanation.surface: Sly hangers-on of a powerful but uncaring boss hatch a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaselly' suggests sneaky people, but otters are literally weasel relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotters are people who scheme in secret, so conspirators.

clue.text: Leave city's wet environment

indicators.note: environment means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: damp means wet
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Get away from the city's soggy surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the City, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly.

clue.text: Church's induction of Reverend Jenny perhaps causes deep division

indicators.note: an induction brings someone in, so the minister and donkey go inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

explanation.surface: A church causes a deep rift by inducting a woman vicar called Jenny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name but is a female donkey; 'causes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier, a deep split.

clue.text: Failing to turn away lost student

indicators.note: lost says a letter goes missing from the word before

parts.note: to deflect is to turn something aside
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student who has given up is turned away for failing.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars, hence a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a flaw or shortcoming, a failing.
